text.p: -- Donaldson, Lufkin cut its ratings on 3Com Corp and U.S. Robotics Corp after announcement of their proposed merger, due to concerns integration issues may take time to sort out and the discounted price paid for Robotics, market sources said.

-- According to a report which was provided by a source to Reuters, DLJ analyst Eric Buck cut both stocks to market perform from buy based on his belief that the deal "substantially constrains the upside potential in USRX shares."
-- The report went on to state that, "Simultaneously, we are reducing our rating on 3Com to market perform from buy."
-- The analyst was not available to confirm the ratings changes.

-- But the sources said the DLJ analyst joined other analysts in complaining the $6.6 billion stock offer for U.S. Robotics represents a significantly discounted multiple compared with where the stock has historically traded.
-- The share offer announced Wednesday evening is roughly 20 times the coming year's earnings expectations, even though Robotics has been typically traded at a multiple 25 times earnings.

-- U.S. Robotics stock was trading up 1-3/4 at 62-3/4 in early trading Thursday, a level significantly below the $68-1/4 contemplated in the deal's terms, which would give Robotics holders 1.75 shares of 3Com stock -- with each share of 3Com valued at $39.
-- 3Com stock was off three points at 36. Volume in both issues was extremely active.
